author: Pink@09
title: Character designs and end game
content:
Wuthering waves is a pretty good game to play. The pity system is easy to understand and isn’t too high. The gameplay itself if really good and is never boring. Despite Wuthering waves being a good game on paper, there’s some big issues that make it hard to enjoy at times. For starters,the character designs are either mid at best, bad, or rarely amazing. A lot of the designs seem to lean more towards sexualizing female characters rather than making them look appealing  and interesting. There’s a big lack of male characters which I find weird because when the game first came out it advertised many male characters and a mostly even male to female character ratio. Over time seeing men in the game has become more and more rare and when they are released, they aren’t as useful as the female characters and seem to have less thought put behind them. There’s also not a lot of four stars in the game making it hard to save and making team building not free to play friendly. Because the four stars in the game tend to be very useless, most teams need to be built to perfection with costly investments in order to complete end game content. I have multiple characters in the game which are built almost perfectly, I don’t have all of their premium teams which makes endgame content so difficult to complete. For example in the game mode whimpering waste, if the player doesn’t have the newest and well built characters, the chance of getting any good rewards are slim as there are a select few characters that can beat the end game mode. In tower of adversity, the middle tower is also difficult to complete with the time given, forcing the player to either invest even more in a team, or get a new one. Characters are replaced frequently with others and team flexibility is lacking. Over all, the game has changed a lot since it first released. The rewards aren’t as appealing as they used to be, the character designs aren’t always the best, the game is getting more difficult and less free to play friendly, the story pacing and telling isn’t that good, and building teams isn’t as fun as it used to be. Characters are hard to skip and it feels like skipping one completely alters how the rest of the game will be played. 

The game isn’t bad especially compared to others but, as a day one player since launch, i find it difficult to stay engaged and enjoy it like i used to. The game is still fun however improvements should definitely be made with endgame content difficultly, free to play teams and flexibility, and rewards.

author: appalachianmountains
title: I love WuWa but…
content: Honestly, I love this game! As someone who’s played Genshin Impact, Honkai Impact 3rd, and Reverse 1999, this game was just as good as those. From the characters designs, VAs, and gameplay, Kuro really outdid themselves there. HOWEVER, I feel that there are some areas where they are lacking in. For example, male characters, 4 star characters, and story. Now, it’s no surprise that there will always be more female characters than male characters in gacha games, but it’s quite disappointing that there’s barely any in this game. I love female characters as much as male characters. However, when there’s very little male characters in the game and in the story itself, it really makes you wonder the point of adding male characters at all. I get that they’re try to target a certain audience and that’s fine. But if they’re trying to target another audience, I’d suggest if they put more effort into it. Another thing is why isn’t there a lot of 4 stars? I’m honestly not sure but it’s unfortunate and I do hope that they add more in the near future. But the most disappointing thing is how the story quest usually revolves around one singular playable female character. Of course, it’s one thing that they barely have any male characters that are significant to the story, but it’s another when you don’t have past characters we’ve seen. I suppose Kuro loves side lining past characters but it’s definitely makes the experience less enjoyable and interesting. I am hopeful that they’ll fix these issues but I’m honestly not sure. And if they don’t know how to do it, then they should look at Genshin Impact, HSR, and Reverse 1999 for help. Those games already got it figured out. Needless to say, this game is REALLY fun to play and has LOTS of potential to keep getting better!

author: Noidea1356
title: Story and gender ratio
content:
The story feels way to rover centered. None of the characters interact with each other. In 2.7 all of the characters in Rinascita were there, which could have had a lot of more dynamics and character interactions. Yet they were all standing in a circle facing Rover.

There could be events where characters talk to eachother and not just having text saying “we are really good friends” the events not being rover centered.

Also, when a character banner leaves, the character is gone, seeing the character no more in the story and instead seeing the new shiny new character. Like with Chisa, I hate how Chisa was managed, Chisa seemed like an interesting character and could have been with Rover more to flesh out the rest of her story more, not the whole story obviously. But once you had gotten to Lahai Roi, you got nothing more than optional dialogue and told the netting went well. Even though she has been gone for 20 YEARS.

You cannot connect with a character by spending time with them and just blow them off and forget about them, especially after having a unique concept and story. Because not everyone will be attracted to Meta or flashy animations. Some people want to connect to the character. And some people are interested in their story and how it will go and play.

The story could feel so much more alive with more dynamics and every answer being rover.

Same goes for the way the stories happen. It’s always 1. Meet the character 2. Get to know them 3. Find out they have a problem 4. fix that problem 5. Heartfelt moment. It’s not a bad way for a story to go, but for almost every character, it has been that way, and it is getting repetitive and making the story boring.

title: The Best Open-World RPG I've Played
content:

Wuthering Waves is one of the best open-world action RPGs I've ever played. The combat is incredibly smooth, fast-paced, and rewarding, with every Resonator feeling unique and satisfying to master. The exploration is fun thanks to the parkour movement, beautiful environments, and hidden secrets around every corner.
The character designs are stunning, and the story continues to get better with each update, introducing memorable characters and emotional moments. The soundtrack perfectly matches every region and battle, making the world feel alive.
As a free-to-play player, I also appreciate how generous the game is with rewards and how enjoyable it is to progress without spending money. Between the engaging events, challenging endgame content, and frequent updates, there's always something to look forward to.
If you're looking for an action RPG with amazing combat, gorgeous visuals, and an ever-expanding world, Wuthering Waves is absolutely worth playing. Highly recommended!

author: Everyone’s favorite <3
title: The best gacha game I’ve played
content:
I have played a bunch of other gacha games, some are good and some are bad, I’ve seen my fair share of gacha games, but never like Wuthering Waves. Wuthering Waves has beautiful story telling and amazing graphics and scenery.

The characters are so appealing to look at and they’re not an eyesore unlike some other games where they’re bold and flashy and hard on the eyes.

Their gacha system is honestly really fair, yes you can still lose your 50/50 but it’s so easy to farm for pulls! And you can’t lose your 50/50 on weapon banner!

The exploration is fun with the flight, motorcycle and grapple mechanics makes it more lively in general instead of running around everywhere on foot. I like that how you can run without burning stamina! (Unless you’re in battle.)

However, there are some things that really need to be fixed, the biggest one being the optimization. I actually play on a nice gaming PC and I still have hicks and lags in Lahi-Roi which I find a little bit frustrating, and the amount of storage it eats. So hopefully in the next few updates they’ll fix it!

Overall I feel like that people should try this game if they want something refreshing and new to play, it’s really generous for the new plays and you should take advantage of that!

author: Kishadembrille
title: Stuff you should fix
content:
I think it would greatly improve the experience if players had more control over dialogue options, including the ability to hear characters use stronger language when it fits their personalities and the tone of the story. 

It would make certain scenes feel more authentic and emotionally impactful. I would also love the ability to revisit previous storylines and permanently access past events. Many stories, character interactions, and memorable moments are worth experiencing again without having to search for them elsewhere.

Additionally, it would be nice if banners for important characters remained accessible in some form, especially for characters that players frequently return to or are highly attached to. This would help newer players and long-time fans alike feel less pressured by limited-time availability.

Overall, adding more player freedom, better story preservation, and improved access to favorite characters would make the game feel more immersive, player-friendly, and rewarding in the long term.

I also believe that adding David Martinez from the anime David Martinez as a playable character would be an incredible collaboration. David is one of the most recognizable and beloved protagonists in modern anime-inspired gaming culture, and his story resonates with many fans because of his determination, loyalty, and willingness to sacrifice everything for the people he cares about.

From a gameplay perspective, his cybernetic enhancements could translate into a unique and fast-paced combat style unlike any existing character. Abilities inspired by his Sandevistan could create exciting high-speed movement, aggressive combos, and visually impressive animations that would fit perfectly within Wuthering Waves' action-focused combat system.

Beyond gameplay, a David collaboration would attract both existing fans of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners and new players who may not have tried Wuthering Waves before. It would be a memorable crossover that celebrates two communities while introducing a fan-favorite character into a new world. Overall, I feel that adding David as a playable character would not only be exciting for fans but would also bring fresh gameplay opportunities increased player engagement and one of the most anticipated crossover characters the game could offer.

David is one of the most iconic anime protagonists in recent years, and his popularity has remained strong long after the show's release. His story, personality, and determination left a lasting impression on many fans, making him a character people genuinely care about.

I think he would fit surprisingly well into Wuthering Waves because of the game's fast-paced combat. His cyberware could inspire a unique moveset centered around extreme speed, powerful close-range attacks, and high-risk, high-reward gameplay. Abilities based on the Sandevistan could create some of the most visually impressive combat animations in the game while giving players a completely different playstyle from the current roster.

A collaboration like this would also generate a lot of excitement within both communities. Fans of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners who have never played Wuthering Waves might be encouraged to try the game, while existing players would get the opportunity to play as a character they have admired for years.

Most importantly, David is a character whose story is built around perseverance, ambition, and fighting against impossible odds—qualities that align well with many of Wuthering Waves' themes. Because of that, he would feel like more than just a crossover character; he would feel like a natural addition to the world and its cast.

Wuthering Waves already has a strong foundation with its combat, world-building, and character designs. Expanding player choice, improving access to past content, and making character availability more flexible would elevate the experience even further and strengthen player engagement for years to come.

author: [ CLASSIFIED]
title: Great game with little flaws
content:
Wuthering waves is like good wine, as it ages it only gets better.

I’ve been playing this game since launch and though I have had my own off and on playtime moments. I have grown to love this game. It’s one of the few gacha games on the market that truly feels cinematic in its story telling. Now I won’t lie, the first part of WUWAs story isn’t all that great and I do wish they would remaster that old first arc to get people in better. However once you get to Rinnacita the whole game changes. It feels like you stepped into a new game all together, a 2.0 moment that really set this game on the right path. Everything after has been great and I look forward to more in the future. Here is a short pros and cons list I have to provide feedback.

Pros:

Amazing gameplay- timed dodging and parrying mechs alongside flashy character quirks.

Overall great voice actors-most ENG VAs do a great job during your playtime. 

Expansive world exploring- the worlds or maps are HUGE and there is so much you can find even unknown secret missions.

Uniqueness- they have introduced many new combats like tune break which allows you to do a “finisher like move” when you fill the tune bar on an enemy dealing big damage!

Cons:

Optimization on certain patches has been harsh. I’m not sure what has been happening but for me it’s been mostly auto cutting and stutters on PC and phone.

Some patches have felt lackluster in terms of action, a lot of times the good stuff is kinda pushed on at the end instead of trickled about.

We need more Endgame activities, there are 3 or so in 2026. One being a very annoying clustering combat called whimpering wastes where the enemies constantly run away from you while you are on a timer to kill them. It’s very annoying especially since they don’t fight back.

The story is a mess, the game just drops terminology on you without explaining very well to sound sci-fi. A lot of weird perspective shifting that doesn’t really add to the story and is just brushed off after it happens. 

Voice acting needs direction, many of the characters feel like they have no emotion to  anything they’re saying. 

The ui copies genshin  and honkai star rail nearly to the letter. So many icons and menus are shameless copies. The 5 star pull animation is ripped from honkai Star rail, the textbox for dialogue is ripped from genshin etc.

author: Nigumo
title: A little like Genshin Impact, but...
content:
This game plays a lot like Genshin Impact, yet it has its own style and diversity
 to make it stand apart.

The first notable difference is that the landscaping and environment is completely different than that of Genshin.
This game has more of a mix between a post apocalyptic nightmare and fast landscapes of natural beauty. I'm still exploring.
Meanwhile, Genshin has landscaping that is more whimsical and memorable. 

Where is this game truly excels & sets itself apart is it's combat system. The combat gameplay for this game is insane and I love the way it is cultivated. 

I like the ability to do simple combos, as well as complex ones. Each character has their own flow to master. 
In addition, I love how you can swap-out to your teammates and juggle enemies too.

The cut scenes are done very well, the ambience of the music is very New Age and fitting for the environments.

I feel that this game may also be a little more generous with the GATCHA rolling system.

The characters are done extremely well and I love the gun-shows!!

Really good game and intend to play for a while.

title: The Boss-Slaying Rush You Haven't Felt Since Childhood
content: If you're craving that pure, heart-pounding thrill of mastering brutal bosses like in your old-school gaming days—dodging by a hair, nailing perfect parries, and chaining swaps for epic combos—Wuthering Waves delivers it in spades with its fluid, skill-based combat that's leagues ahead of button-mashers like Genshin. title: Need change
content:
I like this game, but they really need to change some things. First of all, there are barely any male characters. Having more variety would attract a bigger audience. If they really want the game to grow and not stay stagnant, they need to add more male characters, otherwise it’ll just become another generic game. Genshin Impact is still at the top despite all its flaws because from the beginning it had diversity.

Second, please stop making every female character fall in love with the Rover. It’s boring and repetitive.

Third, make the characters interact with people other than the Rover, and also with characters outside their own region. That makes the world feel more alive and realistic. If every interaction only revolves around the Rover, the game starts feeling lifeless and boring.

Fourth, add more playable villain characters. Not every character has to be good. It’s repetitive and takes away excitement from the story. The same goes for the plot always ending with the Rover winning easily. It never feels like they truly struggle, so there’s no tension because players already know everything will turn out fine in the end. There’s never a sacrifice that actually feels meaningful.
